svg.aria-label: QBM-04 · Iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis — ISC, SUF and CIA
svg.text: QBM-04 · Iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis — ISC, SUF and CIA
The upstream dependency of every Fe/S node in the atlas, and where the review's mechanism is most attractive and least tested

g.title: Cellular Fe / S supply tier T2 (verified) quantum class: structural_context Islam2020: The geomagnetic field contributes to efficient iron uptake in Arabidopsis; reducing it to near-null affects root metal reductase activity. [10.3389/fpls.2020.00325] Vigani2021: Geomagnetic-field-dependent modulation of iron-sulfur interplay in Arabidopsis, most pronounced under combined Fe and S deficiency. [10.3390/ijms221810166] Narayana2018: Reduction of the geomagnetic field to near-null affects Arabidopsis root mineral nutrition. [10.1016/j.lssr.2018.08.005] rationale: Note carefully what the cited work does and does not show. Islam 2020 and Vigani 2021 measured iron uptake and Fe-S interplay under altered field conditions — nutritional physiology. Neither measured cluster assembly. This entity is T2 because the field effect is demonstrated for the process it names; the assembly entities above remain T3 because that evidence does not reach them.
Cysteine desulfurase NFS1 (ISC) tier T4 (inferred) quantum class: structural_context AGI: AT5G65720

Scaffold ISU1 (ISC) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: iron_sulfur_2Fe2S nuclei: 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT4G22220 rationale: Holds a transient, solvent-exposed [2Fe-2S] cluster whose assembly involves iron redox chemistry and sulfide transfer. A nascent cluster on a scaffold is more exposed and shorter-lived than a mature one buried in a protein, which makes it a more credible point of perturbation than the finished product.
caveat: Entirely untested. No experiment has measured scaffold occupancy or transfer rate under any magnetic field condition.

Frataxin (FH) tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context AGI: AT4G03240 Turowski2015: Frataxin is localised to both chloroplast and mitochondrion and is involved in chloroplast Fe-S protein function in Arabidopsis. [10.1371/journal.pone.0141443]

Transfer machinery (HSCB, GRXS15) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: iron_sulfur_2Fe2S nuclei: 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT5G06410, AT3G15660 rationale: GRXS15 binds a bridging [2Fe-2S] cluster in its dimeric form, so the cluster is genuinely in transit and solvent-accessible here rather than buried.

NFU carriers (NFU4, NFU5) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: iron_sulfur_4Fe4S nuclei: 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT3G20970, AT1G51390 rationale: Transiently hold clusters destined for aconitase, succinate dehydrogenase and lipoyl synthase — precisely the QBM-01/QBM-05 nodes the review nominates. If assembly were field-sensitive, this is the step that would show it first.

ATM3 / ABCB25 sulfur export tier T4 (reported) quantum class: structural_context AGI: AT5G58270 Lill2006: Cytosolic Fe/S protein biogenesis depends on export of a sulfur-containing intermediate from the mitochondrion. [10.1146/annurev.cellbio.22.010305.104538]

SUF system (plastid assembly) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: iron_sulfur_4Fe4S nuclei: 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT1G08490, AT4G26500 rationale: Builds every cluster in the chloroplast, including PSI's FX/FA/FB and ferredoxin's [2Fe-2S]. It is the single upstream dependency of QBM-02's strongest nodes.

Plastid cluster carriers (CnfU, HCF101) tier T3 (reported) quantum class: iron_sulfur_4Fe4S nuclei: 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT3G24430 Yabe2004: The chloroplastic NifU-like protein CnfU can act as an Fe-S cluster scaffold and is required for biogenesis of ferredoxin and photosystem I. [10.1105/tpc.020511] rationale: The review names CnfU explicitly: Yabe et al. showed the chloroplastic NifU-like protein acts as a scaffold and is required for photosystem I biogenesis, which makes it the direct upstream dependency of QBO:PSI_FES.

CIA system (cytosolic assembly) tier T3 (reported) quantum class: iron_sulfur_4Fe4S nuclei: 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT5G50960, AT4G16440, AT2G26060, AT1G68310, AT5G48120 rationale: The reason this map matters beyond bioenergetics: CIA clients include the enzymes of DNA replication and repair, so an assembly defect reaches genome maintenance, not just ATP supply.

Fe/S client proteins tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: iron_sulfur_4Fe4S, iron_sulfur_2Fe2S nuclei: 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT4G35830, AT5G66760, AT5G13430, AT4G03280, AT1G10960, AT2G20860, AT2G21790 rationale: Collected here so the map can show, in one edge, that a single assembly defect reaches respiration, photosynthesis, the TCA cycle, nitrogen and sulfur assimilation and DNA replication simultaneously. That breadth is the review's argument for why Fe/S biology deserves attention ahead of cryptochrome.

svg.text: Every Fe/S node on QBM-01, QBM-02 and QBM-05 depends on one of these three systems, so a defect here sits upstream of the whole atlas and would
appear as a metabolic lesion well before any visible phenotype. Read the tiers carefully, because they mark a distinction that is easy to blur: the
near-null-field evidence in this area (Islam 2020, Vigani 2021, Narayana 2018) measured iron UPTAKE and Fe-S interplay — nutritional physiology — and is
attached to the Fe/S supply node, which is therefore T2. No experiment in the bibliography applied a magnetic field and measured cluster assembly itself,
so every assembly node remains T3 no matter how attractive the mechanism looks. The single arrow from mitochondrial export to the CIA system is the
reason this map reaches beyond bioenergetics: CIA clients include the DNA replication and repair enzymes, so a mitochondrial lesion propagates to
genome maintenance. Derived from: Figure 3 panel B of Porterfield & Barker, "Plant Responses to Near-Null Magnetic Fields" — expanded to the three
assembly systems and bound to Arabidopsis loci. Node counts by evidence tier: T2=1, T3=7, T4=3. Schematic topology only — no quantitative value is
encoded in this base map; numbers appear only when measured data is projected onto it. NASA OSDR OSD-782 / GLDS-679, GeneLab-processed
differential expression. cesium-137 gamma radiation at 0.1 Gy against non-irradiated controls at matched time. 0.1 gy, 4 timepoints (1 hour, 3 hour, 24
hour, 72 hour). 10 of 10 identifier-bearing nodes received a series (100%); 1 nodes carry no gene identifier and cannot. multi-locus nodes aggregated by
extreme at each timepoint. GeneLab reports log2 fold change directly; no conversion applied. 5 node(s) have loci that disagree in direction at the same
timepoint (HSCB_GRXS15, NFU_CARRIERS, SUF_SYSTEM, CIA_SYSTEM…), so their single trace is the aggregator choosing between genes that are doing
different things — read those per locus, not as a node. 9 node(s) reverse direction during the course (NFS1, ISU1, FRATAXIN, HSCB_GRXS15…), which no
single-contrast overlay can show. Each node is tinted by its most extreme timepoint. A node standing for ONE locus carries a sparkline of its trajectory —
the colour says how far it moved, the line says when. A node standing for SEVERAL carries a per-locus heatmap instead, one row per locus and one
column per timepoint, because an aggregate cannot show a gene family splitting and under a strong perturbation families do split. A node with no
measurement is left unfilled, which is not the same as a measured zero.
